title: Account-aware evidence prioritizer and SLO simulator for security asks
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Large enterprise customers submit security questionnaires, DPAs, and audit requests that vary by account context (region, industry, contract terms). Our current intake is manual and produces long evidence bundles with low signal — engineering and legal time is wasted, SLAs slip, and customers get inconsistent responses.

Goal: Ship a lightweight decisioning and prioritization layer in the intake flow that: 1) uses account metadata (contract type, region, previous evidence, signed DPAs) to rank required evidence, 2) simulates expected SLA/response windows under different routing choices, and 3) returns a prioritized evidence checklist and a confidence score for automated bundling. This reduces manual triage, speeds responses, and feeds the Console with visible SLO tradeoffs for PM/Support.

Scope: This ticket covers product design, acceptance criteria, and a first MVP schema + API/console wireframe. The engineering implementation (background jobs, evidence fetchers, and routing) will be under a follow-up ENG epic.

Out-of-scope: Full automated answers to questionnaire items, enterprise legal sign-off flow, and on-prem evidence connectors for air-gapped customers (these are future work).
acceptance_criteria: Design a data model for account context used by the prioritizer (region, contract type, signed DPAs, last audit date, product deployment mode)
Define priority ruleset (resource list) and mapping to evidence artifacts (SOC2 report, encryption diagrams, DPA clause excerpts, data residency statements)
SLO simulator that, given current team capacity assumptions, estimates response time ranges (fast/typical/slow) and demonstrates trade-off when routing to concierge vs. default queue
Console mock that shows prioritized evidence checklist and a per-item confidence score (low/med/high) and a suggested bundling set
API contract (intake POST -> prioritized checklist response) documented with examples
A small dataset of 20 anonymized past requests and the expected prioritized outputs for eval and QA
success_metrics: Reduce average manual triage time per request by 40% for Tier A accounts within first 3 months
Increase first-response completeness (first bundle includes >=80% of requested high-priority artifacts) from baseline to target
Decrease median SLA breach rate for security asks routed through this flow from X% to Y% (baseline TBD)
Reduce number of follow-up evidence requests per case by 30%
proposal_notes: Use account tags already available in the billing and contract systems (region, enterprise_tier, dpa_signed_date) to seed the prioritizer

Priority rules: (1) contractual must-haves (signed DPAs / regional data residency requirements), (2) audit-level evidence (SOC2/ISO), (3) architectural evidence (network diagrams, KMS configuration), (4) ancillary docs (privacy policy excerpts, third-party subprocessor list)
SLO simulator inputs: current average handler throughput, expected surge multiplier, SLA target (e.g., 7 business days), and optional concierge fast-path capacity
Confidence scoring: heuristic based on matching history + artifact freshness + contract signal; expose as high/medium/low to help human reviewers
Expose an API that returns both prioritized checklist and a human-readable justification for each inclusion to aid reviewers and audits
design_notes: Console: compact evidence card per item with status (available/missing), confidence, last-updated, and linked source (Drive/Confluence/GitHub repo)
Wireframe includes a simulator toggle to show SLA impact of selecting concierge routing vs. default queue
Include ‘explain why’ modal that surfaces which account signals triggered an item (e.g., DPA clause X => include encryption architecture)
risks: Inaccurate or stale account metadata could cause false positives/negatives in prioritization
Legal concerns around automated evidence selection — must be explicit that this is a helper and not a legal determination
Data residency constraints may require us to avoid returning certain artifacts for some accounts; must be surfaced clearly
Implementation complexity if we later need to fetch artifacts from customer-managed stores (out of scope for MVP)
implementation_outline: PM: finalize ruleset and acceptance dataset
Design: produce mockups and microcopy for evidence confidence explanations
Eng (prototype): define intake API schema and a lightweight rules engine that returns prioritized checklist (mocked data)
Legal: review ruleset and UI copy for regulatory correctness
Support: identify 20 representative past requests to use as evaluation cases

By 2026-03-24: design deliverables (console mocks + API spec)
